issues.title: [BugFix][CI] Add Qwen3.8 TP2 IPC coverage and preserve PLE sleep state
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add a four-layer Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TP2 **unpacked IPC** case using the shared structure from #20535, and preserve PLE context across level-2 sleep.

Model configuration lives in `case.py`. `FixedRandomWeightSource` in the existing `weight_source.py` enumerates the text model on the Transformers meta device, generates deterministic BF16 parameters, and materializes the three small PLE integer buffers using Transformers' own initialization rules. The startup reference and IPC updates use the same generator. The Qwen3.8 reference is streamed into 2 GiB checkpoint shards to bound CPU serialization memory; existing cases retain their single-file default.

HF overrides are applied after configuration normalization, so the indexed full-attention layer uses the canonical `indexed_attention` name. Both inference servers retain the conditional-generation architecture and interleaved MRoPE. The reduced case keeps four layers, PLE, 512 experts and the original hidden size/token vocabulary, with a PLE vocabulary base of 4096, head dimension 128 and 64 rotary channels. MTP and image/video inputs are disabled. PLE stays on NPU and each worker has a fixed 4 GiB KV-cache budget.

MRV2 creates the PLE n-gram context offsets inside the discardable weights pool. They were plain model-state tensors, so the existing model-buffer backup omitted them. Registering a nonpersistent model buffer lets the existing level-2 backup restore the same tensor in place. The focused lifecycle regression is retained.

The test entry point is directly under `ipc/` and uses the existing parametrization and IPC runner. Descriptor preparation, model-specific helper files and custom pytest flags are removed; `npu_ipc.py` matches the base implementation. Directly running the new test executes the hardware case. CI workers must provide configuration and tokenizer/processor assets at `/mnt/weight/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`; pretrained checkpoint tensor values are not loaded.

The PR changes **7 files**:
- CI estimated execution time.
- Shared `case.py` and `weight_source.py`.
- `ipc/test_qwen38_ipc.py` and its README.
- `vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/model_state.py`.
- `tests/ut/models/test_qwen4_exp_ple_sleep.py`.

[Configuration and reproduction instructions](https://github.com/Windfeng8/vllm-ascend/blob/e4f7c07628434c021345d8a633097f44ce457009/tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/rlhf/weight_transfer/ipc/README.md).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Qwen3.8 PLE context offsets survive level-2 sleep/wake and live weight updates. The initialization-only buffer alias adds no per-token synchronization.

The reduced CI does not establish correctness for the original 256-wide attention path, full-size PLE tables, or image/video inference.

### How was this patch tested?

Validated commit `e4f7c07628434c021345d8a633097f44ce457009` on two Ascend950DT NPUs, physical devices **4,5**, with the requested CANN environment sourced before all tests.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| TP2 unpacked IPC with PLE/MRoPE, FULL decode graph capture, and two level-2 sleep/update cycles | **1 passed in 171.25 s** |
| Related weight-transfer unit tests and Qwen4Exp model-state/source regressions | **213 passed** |
| Shared-generator CPU metadata check against local checkpoint headers, combining PLE row shards into the meta model's full embedding | **6,247 tensors matched** in name, shape and dtype; **3 PLE integer buffers matched** |
| New test entry-point collection | **1 unpacked case collected** |
| Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format, codespell 2.4.1, markdownlint-cli 0.45.0 | Passed |
| Package initialization, forbidden imports, boolean context managers, long functions, symbolic meta kernels, logger policy, CI timing YAML and Git whitespace | Passed |
| Full `bash format.sh ci` suite | **Not completed**: dependency bootstrap through the configured GitHub SOCKS proxy reached the execution limits while fetching hook repositories; focused checks above completed |

The dummy-loaded signature must differ from the reference. Both IPC updates must exactly match independently startup-loaded weights in generated text and token logprobs. These strict assertions and FULL graphs remain enabled.

Hardware command:

```bash
source /mnt/share/w00893744/cann_b020/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5 python -m pytest -sv --durations=0 -rs \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/rlhf/weight_transfer/ipc/test_qwen38_ipc.py
```

CPU command (register the Ascend model before importing the adjacent QSA model-state tests):

```python
from vllm_ascend.models.qwen4_exp import model
import pytest

raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    "-q",
    "tests/ut/distributed/weight_transfer",
    "tests/ut/models/test_qwen4_exp_ple_sleep.py",
    "tests/ut/models/test_qwen4_exp_spec_cpu_length_sync.py",
    "tests/ut/models/test_qwen4_exp_source_regression.py",
]))
```

Stack: provided CANN b020 installation (CANN 9.3.0), torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7; runtime vLLM `4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5`, Ascend base `77cf58266b084b517a658c19ba2d3c97fec27df9`. A transparent local directory view of the same CANN files avoids recursive version discovery over NFS. Runner helpers and logs remain outside the PR. The primary checkouts were unchanged; unrelated tasks were not terminated and NPUs were not reset.

issues.title: [Bugfix]Rope does not recover after waking up from sleep mode (L2)
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix incorrect outputs after `sleep(level=2)` + `reload_weights` + `wake_up` for models using the MLA/MTP RoPE path (`AscendRotaryEmbedding`).

**Root cause.** `_record_cos_and_sin_cache_interleaved()` derives two detached tensors (`_cos_cache` / `_sin_cache`, `cos_sin_cache.view(-1, 2, hd).repeat(1, 1, 2).chunk(2, dim=1)`) and caches them in **module-level globals** in `vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py`. Because `.repeat()` materializes real storage, they are allocated inside `NPUWorker.load_model()`'s `CaMemAllocator.use_memory_pool(tag="weights")` scope, so they land in the `weights` pool. But:

- they are not `nn.Parameter`/`nn.Buffer`, so `NPUWorker.sleep`'s level-2 CPU backup  (`model.named_buffers()`) cannot see them, and `reload_weights` does not restore  them either (`vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py:250`, `:286`);
- `allocator.sleep(offload_tags=())` (level 2) passes an empty tuple, so nothing in the  pool is offloaded — every allocation is `unmap_and_release`d with no CPU backup  (`vllm_ascend/device_allocator/camem.py:209-222`), so their physical pages are
  released and `wake_up()`'s `create_and_map()` only remaps the VA, it does not restore contents;
- the cache guard is `if _cos_cache is not None: return`, which is independent of  content, so the tables are **never rebuilt**.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No

### How was this patch tested?

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

issues.title: [BugFix][WeightTransfer] Fix DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision reload across sleep and wake
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Adds a one-card DeepSeek-V4 Flash Vision NPU IPC weight-transfer lane and fixes the sleep → wake → layerwise reload → graph replay path. This follows #18630 and reuses the already-merged Worker `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` mechanism from #18838.

The source branch starts directly at upstream main commit `19c2f7a7cb1504d4624620ea59d6c7fa9eadc422`; the target is **vllm-project/vllm-ascend:main**. The contributor fork only hosts the source branch.

### The fixes

1. **Use upstream loading primitives.** HF names are translated by vLLM `WeightsMapper`; a streaming generator expands fused expert tensors. Packed IPC accumulates chunks and calls `load_weights` once per complete update, before native `finalize_layerwise_reload`. Unpacked IPC keeps its existing loading path.
2. **Use Worker buffer and parameter restoration.** Existing RoPE buffers use the native level-2 buffer backup. Weightless RMSNorm identity tensors are registered as nonpersistent aliases to their original storage so the same mechanism restores them. There are no model-specific boot-time CPU snapshots or post-reload reinitialization hooks.
3. **Retain current checkpoint-backed values explicitly.** `tid2eid`, `bias_vl`, `e_score_correction_bias` and `attn_sink` use the existing `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` option when the sender omits them. They are not automatically frozen: full updates still replace their values. Vision/correction biases have deterministic zero defaults for dummy startup.
4. **Keep native sleep memory behavior.** The normal CaMem weights pool releases physical memory and remaps the reserved virtual addresses on wake. Ordinary allocator cache is cleared before remapping. No persistent weights pool is added.
5. **Invalidate the vision sentinel cache at its owner.** `load_weights` clears the concatenated marker cache so subsequent image forwards use current marker values. HF processor call compatibility and the upstream PCP helper relocation are handled at their existing call sites.
6. **Limit the reload patch to accounting exclusions.** The small compatibility patch updates upstream skip sets in place for runtime buffers/shared aliases. Exclusion alone neither freezes nor preserves parameter values. There is no global meta-materialization override or zero-fill wrapper; the patch registry explains its removal condition.

The refactor reduces the net PR from **28 to 16 changed files**, including **13 to 9 production files**. RoPE implementations, the HCCL engine, production environment variables and unrelated shared test matrices are restored to the historical base. Full-update and retention integration tests share one standalone vision module.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new public Python API or CLI option. Frozen-parameter callers must select served-model names using the existing retention option and omit those parameters from the sender payload. Normal sleep can release the weights pool; retained parameters and runtime buffers still require CPU backups.

Packed IPC buffering applies across models. Cache cleanup before wake may add latency; no performance improvement is claimed.

## How was this patch tested?

One physical NPU (device 3), TP=1, BF16; DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp reduced to **4 text layers, 2 vision layers and 8 experts**. Maximum length 1024, memory utilization 0.45, block size 32. Model Runner V2 uses `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture size 1; the eager control uses `NONE`. Vision encoder graphs are disabled in both configurations.

Environment: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, Transformers 5.14.1, triton-ascend 3.2.2, CANN 9.1.0. The local vLLM source is pristine at the commit listed under Regression scope. Retention tests require a vLLM revision exposing `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` and explicitly skip on older versions without it.

```bash
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /path/to/venv/bin/activate
cd /path/to/vllm-ascend
export VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1
export VLLM_RL_TEST_DEVICE_INDEX=3
export VLLM_RL_DSV4_MODEL=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
export VLLM_RL_DSV4_TEXT_LAYERS=4 VLLM_RL_DSV4_VISION_LAYERS=2
export VLLM_RL_DSV4_EXPERTS=8 VLLM_RL_DSV4_MEM_UTIL=0.45
unset VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER VLLM_RL_DSV4_CUDAGRAPH_MODE VLLM_RL_DSV4_MM_ENCODER_GRAPH
python -m pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer_dsv4_flash_vision.py

VLLM_RL_DSV4_CUDAGRAPH_MODE=NONE VLLM_RL_DSV4_MM_ENCODER_GRAPH=0 \
  python -m pytest -sv -k test_retention_with_vision_reload \
  tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/rlhf/state_transitions/test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer_dsv4_flash_vision.py
```

### Result

| Validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full-update + retention, FULL_DECODE_ONLY, packed/unpacked | 4 passed, zero skips/failures (912.06 s) |
| Retention, NONE, packed/unpacked | 2 passed, zero skips/failures (535.61 s) |
| Model, loader, IPC, packed transport and Worker unit tests | 246 passed, zero skips/failures |
| Mypy on the consolidated vision test and 4 modified production modules, Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 | Passed for all three targets |
| Complete repository format check | `bash format.sh ci`: passed, all hooks |

Retention tests cover all **12 selected parameters** (3 `tid2eid`, 4 `bias_vl`, 1 `e_score_correction_bias`, 4 `attn_sink`) for two distinct current-value states. They verify CPU backup hashes, device values and unchanged addresses at reload start/finalize/finish and after KV-cache wake. Test-only poisoning occurs after storage is remapped and before Worker restores CPU copies, proving that restoration works without accessing unmapped memory. Full-update and level-1 controls are included. Text and image generation signatures match independent normal-startup references.

With the standard weights pool, level-2 sleep released approximately **26.96 GiB** in this reduced configuration, and wake restored **46 of 47 allocations** for weights (the remaining allocation for KV cache). These observations validate this memory lifecycle, not a general memory benchmark.

### Regression scope

- **vLLM base used for local validation**: [`c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b), with no local vLLM source changes. CI's automatically selected vLLM commit is recorded separately in the version metadata below.
- **vllm-ascend base**: upstream main commit [`19c2f7a7cb1504d4624620ea59d6c7fa9eadc422`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/commit/19c2f7a7cb1504d4624620ea59d6c7fa9eadc422), which includes #18838. The source branch starts directly from this commit.
- The skip sets are process-global; matching names leave layerwise completion accounting. Relevant loader tests now execute the previously skipped sink-reload cases and cover both upstream accounting behaviors.
- Packed IPC accumulation and pre-wake cache cleanup affect their shared paths; related transport and Worker unit tests are included.
- Git merge compatibility against official main `8237ee6d690d1399bc6eb48ef5977ac2bd470f3f` was checked cleanly; the runtime runs use the historical base plus this PR, not the synthetic merge tree.
- Multi-card/HCCL hardware, full-size checkpoints, FP8 and broad performance benchmarks were not run.
- Existing dependency/deprecation and producer-shutdown IPC warnings remain visible in logs. The two hardware logs contain 410 HTTP responses, all `200`, and zero `Failed to load weights` messages. Four evidence JSON files record hashes, addresses, boundary checks and reference signatures.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Packed/unpacked full updates, hash/non-hash routing, two current-value states, level-2 retention, full-update and level-1 controls.
- [x] **Regression test**: Native Worker restoration, repeated loader updates, runtime-buffer aliases and marker-cache invalidation.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: No hardware timeout/failure injection was performed.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Actual hashes, pointers and text/image signatures against independent startup references.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: No broad benchmark; sleep memory observations and shared-path cleanup overhead are documented above.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab

issues.title: [Feature][Ops] Gather RoPE cos/sin rows from the contiguous flat base
issues.body:
## Why

Every MTP draft step calls `get_cos_and_sin_mla(positions)` to gather RoPE cos/sin rows. On NPU, indexing the **strided per-half views** (`_cos_cache[positions]`, `_sin_cache[positions]`) makes `aclnnIndex` materialize the **entire cache table** on every lookup, while the effective payload is only `bs * rotary_dim * 2` bytes:

- 1M-row BF16 cache => ~134 MB written / ~250 MB read per lookup, ~420 us each;
- with MTP K=5 that is **12 full-cache materializations per decode step** (2 lookups x 6 forwards), ~4.2 ms/step (~5.7% of the step period) on GLM-5.2 DP16 x TP2.

(GPU keeps lazy views; the NPU aclnn path does not, so the row gather degenerates into a full-table copy.)

## What

Register a contiguous **flat view of the interleaved base table** at registration time (`_cos_sin_flat`, where `_cos_cache[i] == flat[2i]` and `_sin_cache[i] == flat[2i+1]`) and gather rows from it (`flat[positions*2]` / `flat[positions*2+1]`). The flat base is contiguous, so the same row gather is a plain copy (~10 us):

- the fast path is **unconditional** — no config switch. The fix is zero-risk (bitwise identical) and benefits every model on the interleaved-registration path (DeepSeek-V3.2 family, GLM, Kimi, ...);
- the legacy strided gather remains as the fallback for registrations that do not provide the flat view (the non-interleaved `_record_cos_and_sin_cache` path resets it to `None`);
- the flat view shares storage with the registered derived buffers, so the sleep-mode wake restore that rebuilds them in place covers it as well.

## Correctness

**Bitwise identical** to the legacy path: same physical storage, same rows, integer-only index arithmetic (`positions * 2` / `+ 1` on int indices), pure byte copy, identical out-of-bounds domain (`2p < 2N ⟺ p < N`). Proven by unit tests (`tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_flat_gather.py`): flat-vs-fallback bitwise equality (duplicates / empty / boundary positions / `use_cache` path), plus registration semantics (storage sharing with the derived buffers, first-wins, non-interleaved override resets the flat view).

## Performance

Measured on GLM-5.2 (2x Atlas A3, 32 dies, DP16 x TP2, EP32, MTP K=5): removes **12 full-cache materializations per decode step (~4.2 ms/step)**; each lookup becomes ~10 us regardless of cache size, reversing the size sensitivity of the legacy path (whose cost was proportional to the full 1M-row table, independent of batch/context).

## Testing

- [x] `py_compile` + structural assertions for touched files
- [x] New UT: `tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_flat_gather.py`
- [x] NPU server validation (trace assertion: `aclnnIndex_SliceAiCore_Slice` on the rope lookup path 12/step -> 0; draft token sequence bit-identical vs legacy path)

Measured on GLM-5.2 (2 x A3, 32 dies, PD disaggregation, DP2 x TP16, EP32, MTP K=5):

**The ITL is optimized by ~3.5ms**

**NOTE:** This is the first of two PRs splitting #18219 (the two features are file-orthogonal and independently revertable). The sibling PR (multistream MTP metadata overlap) will be submitted separately; #18219 can be closed once both land.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab
